item.title: China initiates steps to explore the Jupiter system
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
The China National Space Administration has begun to take concrete steps to prepare for one of its ambitious interplanetary expeditions — the Tianwen 4 that aims to explore the Jovian system. The administration announced on Friday that the robotic probe is set to orbit Jupiter and land on its second-largest moon, Callisto, for close observation and survey. To achieve these goals, the Lunar Exploration and Space Engineering Center of the administration started on Friday soliciting research and development proposals for scientific equipment that mission planners have decided to put on the Tianwen 4 spacecraft. According to the center, the Tianwen 4 will be equipped with 12 scientific payloads on its orbiter and lander. The orbiter will carry 10 payloads for two core research areas. Space environment detection tools — including a magnetic field and wave detector, particle analyzers, a soft X-ray spectrometer and a far-ultraviolet imager — will explore Jupiter’s multi-band auroras, the interaction between its vast magnetosphere and solar wind, and how solar particles spread through the outer solar system. Remote sensing apparatus such as cameras, a laser altimeter, a visible-infrared imaging spectrometer and a gamma-ray spectrometer will map Callisto’s terrain, analyze its surface composition and detect radioactive elements. The Callisto-bound lander will bring two in-situ measurement instruments — a surface composition analyzer that will identify materials at the landing site via Raman spectroscopy, and a surface magnetometer that will take on-site magnetic readings. Combined with orbital data, the surface magnetometer will help separate ionospheric and interior magnetic signals, offering key insights into Callisto’s internal structure and its potential subsurface ocean. The center noted that it encourages overseas institutes to join programs led by Chinese organizations or submit their own proposals. According to information previously published by Chinese space mission planners, the Tianwen 4 probe is scheduled to be launched by a Long March 5 heavy-lift carrier rocket from the Wenchang Space Launch Center in Hainan province around 2029. To date, humankind still lacks comprehensive knowledge of the Jovian system and has performed only a handful of exploration operations. Therefore, the gas giant planet is full of opportunities for science and discovery, Zhang Rongqiao, a top mission planner at the CNSA, said. While Jupiter, the largest planet of our solar system, has been known for a long time, the first detailed observations of it were made by Galileo Galilei in 1610 with a small telescope. The first spacecraft to visit Jupiter was the United States’ Pioneer 10 in 1973. Since then, this planet has been visited by several passing probes and orbiters. The most recent Jovian mission was launched by NASA in October 2024. The spacecraft, named Europa Clipper, is the first mission designed to conduct a detailed study of Jupiter’s icy moon Europa. The spacecraft is traveling 2.9 billion kilometers to reach Jupiter in April 2030. Contact the writer at zhaolei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Suspect dies after shooting north of White House
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
WASHINGTON -- A shooting at a gym about 1.6 km north of the White House early Thursday left one person dead and four others injured. The suspected gunman later died, US media reported. Police were in contact with the suspect by phone while he was barricaded inside a nearby apartment building, NBC News reported. Officers later found him dead with an apparently self-inflicted gunshot wound. Police believe the suspect had a "conflict" related to the apartment building, according to the NBC News report. "The barricade has concluded. The scene is safe. Significant traffic closures remain in place," the Metropolitan Police Department, the primary law enforcement agency for the District of Columbia, said in an updated post on the social media platform X. Earlier Thursday, the department said in a post on X that officers were responding to an "active shooting" near 15th and P Streets and urged the public to avoid the area. According to the Gun Violence Archive, 408 mass shootings had been recorded in the United States so far this year as of Thursday, resulting in more than 100 deaths.

item.title: Huang's exit puts Nvidia leadership, AI policy in focus
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down as Nvidia's chief executive on Thursday, four days after admitting to an extramarital affair, leaving the chipmaker facing a leadership transition and raising questions about the direction of the AI industry and US chip export policy. Nvidia's board announced that Huang, the company's co-founder, had resigned as president, chief executive and a board member, effective immediately. Colette Kress, executive vice-president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive while the board considers internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement. The departure followed media reports alleging three extramarital affairs, including two involving Nvidia employees. The other woman, whom Huang admitted to having an affair with, was a Chinese businesswoman. Following the news, Nvidia shares fell as much as 14 percent before recovering most of their losses to close 4.3 percent lower at $166.19, leaving the company with a market value of $4.01 trillion. The leadership change has created uncertainty for a company central to the AI industry, but its immediate implications may be more limited than the initial market reaction suggested, Ker Gibbs, former president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai, told China Daily. "Jensen Huang played an important role in maintaining customer relationships, but demand for Nvidia's products remains strong, and his departure doesn't change that," said Gibbs, author of The Fragile Dragon: China's Strengths and the Limits to its Power. He said the stock was down about 30 percent from its October peak, although much of the decline preceded the scandal and reflected broader concerns about AI valuations. The reaction so far has largely been specific to Nvidia, Gibbs said, noting that the broader market and other chip stocks rose this week. The forces driving AI development are diverse and well-funded, he added, and do not depend on one company's leadership. The more consequential change could emerge in Washington, where Huang had been a prominent advocate against tight restrictions on chip sales to China. Lawmakers have called for investigations into whether national security was compromised. House Republicans were discussing possible congressional testimony with Huang sometime this month, The New York Times reported, although no appearance has been scheduled. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting semiconductor chip exports to China. Analysts at SemiAnalysis, a Silicon Valley AI research firm, said Huang's departure could accelerate that shift. "AI and chip restrictions on China are going to ramp now much faster with the biggest defender Jensen, gone," Dylan Patel and three other analysts wrote in a report. Patel, the firm's founder and chief executive, warned that poorly shaped restrictions could damage US interests by disrupting supply chains and weakening the development of open-source AI models, which Huang had championed. The report said major US technology companies depend on Chinese companies in their supply chains, while American startups benefit from research published by Chinese companies, students and independent researchers using those chips. "The US open source ecosystem and many startups rely on Chinese AI models. This is significantly impaired with Jensen gone and the China hawks winning," the analysts wrote. Regarding supply chain, Gibbs said, Nvidia's ties with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co and other partners in Taiwan are deeply institutional and unlikely to be disrupted by a leadership change. Instead, he expects closer scrutiny of distributors and data center operators in Southeast Asia, alongside tighter enforcement against the diversion of chips to China. "For Nvidia specifically, the company has lost its most effective advocate for access to the Chinese market," Gibbs said. "Under interim leadership and intense scrutiny from the FBI and Congress, I would expect Nvidia to become far more cautious." That could mean less lobbying against export controls, tighter oversight of distributors and a lower public profile on China, he said. The regulatory pressure will also shape the challenges facing Kress and whoever succeeds her. Gibbs said he would watch next week's earnings and forward guidance for signs of customer hesitation, the selection of a permanent chief executive, the findings of investigations and any changes to export controls. "The biggest challenge for the interim CEO, and her eventual successor, will be rebuilding trust with regulators," he said. For startups, dependence on Nvidia rests primarily on its products and software ecosystem, which are continuing through the transition, Gibbs said. However, Nvidia could slow its strategic investments under interim leadership, while investors may scrutinize startups with exposure to China or Southeast Asian data center operators more closely. Huang's departure also removes a business leader with unusual access to the White House, potentially changing the balance of voices influencing US technology policy. High-profile executives have long provided an additional channel of communication between the US and China, Gibbs said, although their commercial responsibilities differ from those of officials charged with national security. "He was also an important voice that ran counter to the national security hawks. His absence will certainly shift that balance," he said. For companies operating across the two countries, the episode highlights the need for governance and institutional relationships that can withstand pressure, Gibbs said. Personal access can become a vulnerability when business spans countries engaged in strategic competition. Even so, he said Huang's departure would not necessarily undermine Nvidia's competitiveness. "He's been the sole face of the company externally, but there are a lot of smart and capable people who have a hand in running a company like Nvidia," Gibbs said. "It's hard to imagine Nvidia collapsing without him."

item.title: 'Miracle' metropolis now a global magnet
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
For Canadian entrepreneur Luc Junior Denommee, one of Shenzhen's greatest attractions is not its futuristic skyline or the technology giants that call it home. It is the ease with which an idea can become a product. In Huaqiangbei, the sprawling electronics marketplace at the heart of the city in Guangdong province, almost everything an entrepreneur needs — from batteries and electronic components to product designers, precision machining services and logistics providers — can be found within easy reach. The concentration of suppliers and expertise means that an idea can move from the drawing board to a working prototype with remarkable speed, an advantage that impressed Denommee when he first arrived in Shenzhen in 2007. "Every month, there's something new about the memory, about design. Here is the capital of electronics, I would say, in the world." Nearly two decades later, the marketplace continues to surprise him with new products and technologies. But Shenzhen has given Denommee something beyond business opportunities: a sense of belonging. "I feel more at home in Shenzhen than anywhere else in the world," he said. "Here, I'm really part of an ecosystem which is growing. I feel I am living. I am not surviving."

item.title: What APEC has to do with your fruit plate
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
It's November, and Chilean cherries continue to arrive in China. In 2008, Chilean cherries were officially granted zero-tariff access to the Chinese market. Once a luxury item, they now reach Chinese dinner tables at lower prices and in fresher condition, thanks to direct maritime routes, streamlined logistics, and faster customs clearance. The cherry trade not only enriches Chinese dinner tables — it also sustains Chilean livelihoods. This is something the APEC has been doing for more than 30 years — advancing free and open trade and investment in the Asia-Pacific. Watch the video to see what APEC has to do with ordinary people like us.

item.title: Former UNESCO chief: High expectations for APEC Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov 18 to 19. Irina Bokova, former director-general of UNESCO, told China Daily that Shenzhen's transformation from a fishing village into a bustling metropolis with universities, technology, culture, economy, and finance is remarkable. As a green city and a city of learning, Shenzhen exemplifies China's inclusive development. Amid global turbulence, Bokova hopes this APEC meeting will foster dialogue, dispel mistrust and bring economies together to tackle world challenges. Watch the video!

item.title: Asia-Pacific needs digital bridges, not 'digital fences'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
During an interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Ong Tee Keat, president of the Belt and Road Initiative Caucus for Asia Pacific in Malaysia, stresses inclusive digital supply chain finance, local-currency settlement and inclusive credit — rejecting "small yards and high fences"— plus capacity building so the digital dividend leaves no one behind. During the interview, Ong says China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 putting digital trade and sustainable innovation at the core of regional integration. More supportive measures will release a great regional market potential. Ong adds that interoperable digital frameworks let small traders access regional value chains through QR payments, e-commerce and paperless customs. But compliance burdens and tech disruption can marginalize grassroots entrepreneurs and uneven digital readiness makes coordination hard. Therefore, the region needs more coordinative efforts to solve the problems. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Pan Yixuan)

item.title: Shenzhen: A gateway to openness
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
From a fishing village to a hub of innovation, Shenzhen's remarkable transformation reflects China's extraordinary journey of reform and opening-up. As the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaches, the city continues to embrace the world with open arms, echoing President Xi Jinping's words: "China's door to the world will not close; it will only open wider and wider."

item.title: Mutual respect key to cooperation, says ex-ambassador
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Mutual respect and multilateralism are essential to managing international differences and strengthening cooperation, former Chinese ambassador to France Kong Quan said on Wednesday at the Paris Peace Forum, stressing that China's development offers opportunities rather than threats to other countries. Speaking at a session titled "Making Sense of China's Global Role and Impact", Kong, who is also a standing member of the China Economic and Social Council, said countries should recognize their differences in political systems and stages of development while seeking common ground through dialogue. "The diversity of the world is what makes humanity beautiful," he said. "China has never asked any country to embrace all its policies. What we want is to be understood on the basis of China's realities, in all their complexity and diversity." Kong identified mutual respect as one of four principles guiding China's approach to international relations, alongside responsibility, multilateralism and cooperation based on respect for sovereignty. Regarding multilateralism, Kong said China supports making international governance fairer and more equitable rather than establishing exclusive blocs. Global South countries remain underrepresented in international affairs despite their growing importance, he said. "The goal is neither to replace the United Nations nor to ask countries to choose sides, but to give more countries the opportunity to participate in discussing international rules and sharing the benefits of development," he said, referring to China's support for BRICS and other South-South cooperation mechanisms. Mauricio Favero, head of the Special Office for Diplomatic Planning at Brazil's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said multipolarity must be accompanied by multilateralism. "Multilateralism anchored in dialogue, negotiation and peaceful coexistence is basic," he said, adding that the challenges facing humanity demand a collective action. Kong said national sovereignty and international cooperation are not mutually exclusive. "China respects the sovereignty of all countries, as well as their legitimate security concerns," he said. Addressing emerging challenges in AI, data governance and critical technologies, Kong called for distinguishing genuine security risks from generalized and politicized security anxieties. "We support a greater role for open-source communities and open standards, which can make innovation more transparent, more inclusive and less monopolized by a minority," he said. Kong also called for strengthening technological capabilities in developing countries to prevent them from being marginalized in the latest wave of technological transformation. Concluding his remarks, Kong said China is not and will never be a danger to anyone, but an opportunity for development and cooperation. "It is not a rival, still less an adversary, as some claim, but rather a reliable partner," he said, noting that China remains consistent in its strategy and actions. zhangzhouxiang@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for unity to carry on Sun Yat-sen's legacy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
President Xi Jinping called on Chinese people at home and abroad on Thursday to unite more closely, carry forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy and work together for national rejuvenation, turning into reality the great dream pursued by generations of Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi also urged people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and Chinese people worldwide to join hands in opposing "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces and promoting the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth, attended by about 3,000 people at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, was born in 1866 and led the Revolution of 1911, which ended thousands of years of imperial rule in China. He died in 1925. Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution who devoted his life to transforming China and made outstanding contributions to its people and the Chinese nation. Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators and faithful successors to Sun's revolutionary cause, Xi said. Over the past century and more, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the nation's history, he added. The railways, roads, communications networks, water conservancy projects, canals, ports, factories and mines that Sun envisaged in his Plans for National Reconstruction have not only become reality, but have been surpassed in scope and scale, he said. China now ranks as the world's second-largest economy and has achieved moderate prosperity in all respects, Xi said, adding that these achievements would bring solace to Sun. The best way to remember Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing efforts to build a great country and rejuvenate the nation, he said. Xi said that Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation. His strong desire and firm resolve for national reunification have continued to enlighten, educate and inspire Chinese people at home and abroad, Xi said. Realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. Taiwan's realities, as well as the interests and feelings of Taiwan compatriots, would be fully taken into account, he said, while stressing that no room would be left for "Taiwan independence" secessionist activities in any form. Taiwan's future lies in national reunification, and the interests and well-being of Taiwan compatriots are tied to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, he added. Xi also called for carrying forward Sun's patriotism and lifelong dedication to building a strong and prosperous China. Praising Sun's devotion to the people, he stressed the need to put the people first, serve them wholeheartedly and make solid progress toward well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. He also urged Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's commitment to unity, Xi stressed the need to unite all forces that can be united, consolidate and develop the broadest possible patriotic united front, and pool strength to advance Chinese modernization. Sun's vision extended beyond China's borders, Xi said. Sun believed that a stronger China would bear a major responsibility to the world and that its transformation would help bring a brighter future for humanity. On Thursday morning, a ceremony to pay respect at a Sun Yat-sen cenotaph in Beijing's Biyun Temple was organized to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn
